questions.question: The famous UNESCO heritage site, Robben Island served as the political prison of which of the following leaders?
questions.solution:
__
 
• **Robben Island**__ is an** island in Table Bay**, Cape Town, South Africa.
 
• **Nelson Mandela was imprisoned** there for 18 of the 27 years.
 
• He was later awarded the **Nobel Prize for Peace and was elected in 1994 as President **of South Africa.
 
• Nelson Mandela International Day (or Mandela Day) is an annual international day in honor of Nelson Mandela, celebrated each year on 18 July, Mandela's birthday. 
 
• The day was officially declared by the United Nations in November 2009, with the first UN Mandela Day held on 18 July 2010.

questions.question: Which of the following is a monetary policy tool used by RBI to control inflation?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Repo rate**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Repo rate is the rate at which the** central bank of a country lends money to commercial banks**. 
 
• Repo rate is used by monetary authorities to control inflation.
 
• RBI, in its sixth bi-monthly monetary policy of FY 2019-20, has kept the **repo rate unchanged at 5.15%**.

 
 

 Monetary Policy tool__
 __Description__
 
 

 
 
Repo Rate

 
 
 
The (fixed) interest rate at which the Reserve Bank provides overnight liquidity to banks against the collateral of government and other approved securities under the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF).

 
 
 

 
 
Reverse Repo Rate

 
 
 
The (fixed) interest rate at which the Reserve Bank absorbs liquidity, on an overnight basis, from banks against the collateral of eligible government securities under the LAF.

 
 
 

 
 
Marginal Standing Facility

 
 
 
A facility under which scheduled commercial banks can borrow an additional amount of overnight money from the Reserve Bank by dipping into their Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) portfolio up to a limit at a penal rate of interest

 
 
 

 
 
Open Market Operation

 
 
 
 Open market operations are the sale and purchase of government securities and treasury bills by RBI

questions.question: Typhoid and Tuberculosis are what type of diseases?
questions.solution:
**Concept**:

__
 
• Typhoid and Tuberculosis are Bacterial diseases.
 
• Bacterial diseases include any type of illness caused by bacteria.
 
• Bacterial diseases occur when pathogenic bacteria get into the body and begin to reproduce.
 
• Harmful bacteria may also emit toxins that damage the body.
 
• various bacterial diseases are Cholera, tuberculosis, typhoid, plague, Diptheria, tetanus, whooping cough, etc.

 
 

 
 
**Disease**__

 
 
 
__**Causative Organism**__

 
 
 

 
 
Cholera

 
 
 
Vibrio cholera is the causative organism of the disease Cholera. Cholera is an infectious disease that leads to dehydration.

 
 
 

 
 
Influenza

 
 
 
Myxovirus is the causative organism of the disease Influenza. It can cause the common cold, mumps, and measles in humans.

 
 
 

 
 
**Tuberculosis**

 
 
 
**Mycobacterium **is the causative organism of the disease Tuberculosis. This bacteria affects the lungs and other parts of the body.

 
 
 

 
 
**Typhoid**

 
 
 
**Salmonella bacteria** is the causative organism of the disease Typhoid. It is caused by contaminated water and food with the feces of an infected person.

questions.question: In physics, what is the Hubble constant?

options.text: Unit of measurement that explains the expansion of the universe

questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. __**Unit of measurement that explains the expansion of the universe**__.

 
• American astronomer **Edwin Hubble** (the space telescope was named after him) measured the speed of galaxies and their distance from Earth and obtained the graph.
 
• Hubble's law is a statement of a direct correlation between the distance to a galaxy and its recessional velocity as determined by the redshift. It can be stated as:
 
• **v=Hₒd**, In the equation, v is the velocity of a receding galaxy, d is the distance to the galaxy, and Hₒ is the Hubble's constant.
 
• **Hubble's constant** is approximately **2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ S****⁻¹** if the distance is in 
meters and the speed in meters per second.

questions.question: Which Indian founded the Natal Indian Congress (NIC)?
questions.solution:
Option **2** is correct, i.e. __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

__
 
• In **1894,** Mahatma Gandhi__ founded the **Natal Indian Congress**, of which he himself became an indefatigable secretary.
 
• The Natal Indian Congress (NIC) was an organization formed to fight the discrimination faced by Indians in South Africa.
 
• Gandhi was the first Honorary Secretary of the Congress.
 
• This organization went on to lead many non-violent protests in the cause of discrimination faced not just by Indians but also by native Africans.
